# Relay Gateway — Agent Install Instructions

You are an AI coding agent (Claude Code, Codex CLI, or similar) with shell,
git, and Docker execution access. A user has asked you to install this
project. Follow these steps in order.

## 1. Clone the repository

```
git clone https://github.com/tadeubanzato/message-gateway
cd message-gateway
```

Note: this repository is currently **private**. If the clone fails with an
authentication/permission error, the user (or you, the agent, if you have
GitHub credentials configured) needs to authenticate as a user with access
before cloning will work — do not assume the repo is public.

## 2. Prepare the environment file

```
cp .env.example .env
```

Do not edit `.env` yet — leave it at its defaults for now. It defaults to
`DB_BACKEND=sqlite`, which requires no external accounts and works
immediately.

## 3. Build and start the container

```
docker compose up -d --build
```

Wait for the container to report healthy:

```
docker compose ps
```

If it does not become healthy within a couple of minutes, check logs with
`docker compose logs` and report the failure to the user rather than retrying
indefinitely.

## 4. Connect to the MCP server

Once healthy, the gateway exposes an MCP server at:

```
http://localhost:8010/mcp
```

Connect to it using whatever MCP-client mechanism you have available.

## 5. Run the setup wizard

Once connected, call the wizard tools in this order:

1. `get_setup_status()` — see what's already configured (fresh installs will
   show nothing configured yet).
2. `list_providers("email")`, `list_providers("sms")`, `list_providers("push")`
   — show the user their options for each channel and ask which they want.
3. For each channel the user picks a provider for, call
   `get_setup_instructions(provider)` — this returns which environment
   variables to set and where to obtain the values. **This tool does not
   accept or need secret values as arguments — do not ask the user to paste
   API keys/tokens into this chat.** Instead, tell the user to open `.env` in
   the cloned repo themselves and set the variables it lists.
4. After the user confirms they've edited `.env`, tell them to run:
   ```
   docker compose restart
   ```
   (This project deliberately does not auto-restart itself — do not attempt
   to restart the container via the Docker socket or any other automated
   means on the user's behalf; this was an explicit security decision by the
   project, not an oversight.)
5. Call `check_provider_config(channel)` to verify the new credentials work.
   If it fails, relay the specific error back to the user and offer to
   re-check after they fix it — do not guess at what's wrong.
6. Repeat for each channel the user wants configured. Push/SMS/email are all
   independent — the gateway works with only one or two configured if that's
   all the user needs.

## 6. Confirm completion

Once `check_provider_config` passes for at least the channel(s) the user
cares about, tell the user the gateway is installed and configured, and that
they can now ask you (or any MCP-connected agent) to send notifications via
the `send_notification` tool, or inspect queue status / message history /
dead letters via the operator tools the same MCP server exposes.

## Notes for the agent

- Never write real secret values into any file yourself — the user edits
  `.env` directly. Your role is to explain what's needed and verify it after
  the fact, not to collect or relay credentials.
- If the user's client doesn't support the operations above (no shell, no
  MCP), stop and tell them to use the manual install path documented in
  README.md instead.
